newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends narrowly mixed, still in range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends narrowly mixed, still in range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended narrowly mixed Monday in a very quiet session, with prices stuck in recent technical ranges and many players sidelined waiting for July flows to begin Tuesday.
August finished unchanged at $2.139 per million British thermal units after trading in a narrow 2.5 cent range. Sept settled 0.4 cent lower at $2.136. Others ended steady to up.

"We had some nuke problems and some heat and we should have been able to kick it up and couldn't. Time is running against the bulls, and there's going to be more and more people looking to sell rallies," said one Midwest trader.
While many were sidelined waiting for clearer signs from the cash once July gas starts to flow, traders said activity was likely to remain slow this week ahead of the July 4 holiday.
Temperatures in the South and East are expected to remain above normal this week, with Texas forecast to return to normal later in the week. The Southwest was expected to stay hot for the period.

Chart traders noted a symmetrical triangle formation in August, with support seen along the up trendline in the $2.11 area and trendline resistance pegged at $2.27. More buying was expected at the recent $2.08 low, while further selling should emerge at the recent $2.36 high and the $2.415 contract high.

In the cash Monday, Gulf Coast prices notionally were unchanged to up slightly in the low-to-mid teens. Midcon pipes firmed a couple of cents to the low-$2s. New York city gate gas for July was quoted steady in the mid-$2.40s.
Separately, the 1,250 megawatt South Texas 1 nuclear unit was expected to return to full power later today. The unit was reduced to 69 percent power over the weekend for repairs.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip edged up 0.1 cent to $2.21. NYMEX said 12,289 contracts traded, down sharply from Friday's revised tally of 26,686.

On the KCBT, August closed one-half cent higher at $2.02, while deferreds ended up by one-half. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.5 cent to 11.9 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 134 lots traded, off sharply from Friday's total of 506.
